R0012.title: Cheating Tools / Game Hacks
R0012.definition: Cheating tools refer to illegal programs or script code used in computer games or software, designed to give users unfair advantages or modify program functionality.
R0012.description: Generally includes: cheat programs providing capabilities beyond normal gameplay such as auto-aim and wall hacks; automation scripts that automatically perform specific tasks like resource collection or quest completion without player involvement; and speed hacks that modify game speed to allow faster movement or actions.
R0012.influence: Disrupts the normal operating logic of the application, thereby affecting normal platform operations.

references.title: NetClean 2025 | Police Crack Down on Game Cheat Tools

observables: The client process memory is injected with unknown modules, or exhibits abnormal read/write access to game memory
A single account exhibits precision aiming, consecutive hits, or fixed-rhythm automated actions at speeds beyond human reaction time within a short window
In-game values such as movement speed and skill cooldowns are tampered beyond server-defined thresholds
A cheat process or debugger handle establishes an abnormal attachment to the game process
The account's login device fingerprint co-occurs with characteristic cheat-tool processes

R0012-001.title: Red Packet Grabbing Bot
R0012-001.definition: Using cheating tools/scripts to automatically grab red packets in a fraudulent manner.
R0012-001.description: Mainly used in red packet features of social apps or games such as WeChat and QQ. These tools help users grab red packets the moment they are sent, typically by monitoring chat records and auto-clicking. When a red packet is detected, the tool immediately clicks to grab it at a speed far exceeding human capability.
R0012-001.influence: Undermines platform fairness and disrupts normal user activity order.

references.title: Old Wine in New Bottles: Accessibility Service Abuse by Mobile AI Agents and Unfair Competition

observables: Red packets are grabbed within milliseconds of being released, far faster than the distribution of human click times
A single account maintains a fixed grab latency across multiple red packet sessions, with mechanical timing
Accessibility services or assistive APIs are continuously invoked by a cheat process that monitors chat notifications
Auto-click scripts or simulated-click tools detected on the device are strongly correlated with red packet events
The account continues to grab red packets while in the background or with the screen locked

R0012-002.title: Game Cheating Software
R0012-002.definition: Game cheating software refers to illegal software or scripts used in video games to gain unfair advantages, modify game content, or manipulate game rules.
R0012-002.description: Includes: cheat programs providing capabilities beyond normal gameplay such as auto-aim, wallhacks, and infinite lives; scripts and macros that automatically execute specific operations like auto-casting or auto-resource collection; speed hacks; external modifiers that change game files or memory data; and gold/item generators that create fake in-game currency or items.
R0012-002.influence: Undermines game fairness and in-game economies, harms legitimate player experience, and may cause account, item, and platform revenue losses.

references.title: Shanghai Pudong Dismantles Illegal Game Account Sales Gang

observables: A player's aim accuracy reaches 100% or chains consecutive headshots with reaction times below human physiological thresholds
Character physics parameters such as movement speed and jump height exceed server-configured upper limits
Multiple accounts under the same IP range or device fingerprint share identical cheat signatures with abnormally uniform resource collection rates
Game memory is read or written by an external process, with key values (health, gold, coordinates) showing unauthorized modifications
An account exhibits persistent tracking of targets behind walls or pre-aiming at unseen enemies, consistent with wallhack use
